title: WEST NILE POSITIVE IN XENIA
full_story:
Clay County Health Department confirmed the third West Nile virus (WNV) positive mosquito sample of the 2026 season in Clay County.  The positive sample was collected in Xenia on Thursday and was confirmed through routine testing.

Confirmation of a WNV positive mosquito sample means that the virus is circulating in the community and there is a heightened risk of infection for humans.  Residents are urged to take the necessary precautions to protect themselves from mosquito bites.  It is important to remember the three R’s – reduce your exposure to mosquitoes, repel them by wearing insect repellant, and report areas where mosquitoes typically breed.

WNV is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected mosquito.  Mosquitoes pick up the virus by feeding on infected birds.  The illness is not spread from person-to-person.  Most people infected with West Nile virus show no symptoms.  However, some people may experience fever, nausea, headache, and muscle aches.  Symptoms may last from a few days to a few weeks.  In rare cases, severe illness including meningitis or encephalitis, or even death, can occur.  People older than 50 are at higher risk for severe illness from West Nile virus.

Because WNV generally appears and spreads in Illinois mosquito populations as early as two to six weeks before it is transmitted to humans, monitoring the mosquito populations in our communities helps us predict when humans will be at risk for WNV infection.  Surveillance activities in Clay County include laboratory tests on mosquito batches and responding to concerns of mosquito production sites.

If you would like more information on West Nile virus, contact the Clay County Health Department at 618-662-4406 or visit the website www.healthdept.org.

title: ELM RIVER CHOWDER
full_story:
The Elm River Chowder will be held tomorrow, at the Chowder Grounds.  Cost of the chowder is by donation.  Chowder will be for sale by the bowl with seating available and chowder will also be dipped by the bulk at around 12:30 pm.  Please, do not bring glass or plastic containers.

There will also be pulled pork sandwiches, nachos, hot dogs, pie by the slice or whole, and cold drinks.

The Elm River chowder grounds are either six miles south of Clay City off of Route 50 or four miles east of the Rinard Crossroads off of Route 45, watch for signs.

The Elm River Chowder is an over 100 year tradition, funded entirely by donation.  Vegetable prep will begin at 7 am, volunteers are welcome.  For more information, find the Elm River Chowder on Facebook.

title: INGRAHAM LABOR DAY PICNIC
full_story:
The Annual Ingraham Labor Day Picnic & Tractor Pull is Monday.

With an entry fee of $20.00, the truck pull begins at 9:00 am, followed by the modified, stock, diesel and tractor pulls at 1:00 pm, including the Illinois Stock Pullers Association, the Central Illinois Tractor Pullers Association, and the Illinois Hot Farm Stock Pullers, plus Stock Farm Class and Brush Class Semi Trucks, with the gate admission at $10.00 for adults and $5.00 for children age 6 to 12.

The fish dinner will cost $10.00 per person, and will be prepared and served by the Ingraham Firemen, with serving from 11:00 to 2:00, then vegetable soup will be available at 4:00 pm, either by the bowl at $3.00 each or by bulk sale after 5:00 at $20.00 a gallon, bring your own container.

There will also be a novelty stand, ice cream, treasured baskets, a 50/50 raffle, and more.

title: PALESTINE RODEO
full_story:
The Palestine Rodeo is still on, according to the Palestine Chamber of Commerce, though flood waters have made it hard on campers.

According to chamber members, rising water levels from recent severe weather flooded the campground at Leaverton Park.  Due to this, camping at the park has been cancelled over Labor Day weekend.  They added that the rodeo is still going forward.

All vendors, Main Street activities, as well as the beer tent, will still be up and running as scheduled.  Chamber members apologized for any inconvenience to campers and said that they will be calling all registered campers to ensure they receive the update.

title: LANES REOPENING
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation announced that lanes that have been closed for construction will reopen, where possible, for the Labor Day weekend to minimize travel disruption.

Non-emergency closures will be suspended from 3 pm Friday, to 11:59 pm Monday.

The following lane closures will remain in place during the holiday weekend.  The public can expect delays and should allow extra time for trips through these areas.  Drivers are urged to pay close attention to changed conditions and signs in the work zones, obey the posted speed limits, refrain from using mobile devices and stay alert for workers and equipment.  At all times, please buckle up and drive sober.

In Effingham County on I-57 near the Green Creek Rest Areas north of Effingham; and on I-70 at Altamont; lane reductions will continue.  In Richland County on Illinois Route 130 over the East Fork Fox River about a mile north of Olney; lane reductions continue with traffic controlled by temporary signals.  And in Wayne County on Illinois Route 15 over the Little Wabash River about 6 miles east of Fairfield; lane reductions continue, with traffic controlled by temporary signals.

For more information on IDOT projects, click here or view area construction details on the traveler information map on GettingAroundIllinois.com.

title: FRIENDS OF THE LIBRARY FALL BOOK SALE
full_story:
The Friends of the Flora Public Library Fall Book Sale will be held on Saturday, September 12th from 8 am to 3 pm and the library is seeking donations.

The library needs people to contribute your used books, DVD’s, CD’s and magazines to the sale.  To donate just drop off your items that are in good shape to the front desk.

The Flora Public Library is open Monday through Thursday 1:00 – 8:00 pm, Friday 10:00 am to 6:00 pm and Saturday 10:00 am to 3:00 pm.  The library has a handcart to assist individuals who may be bringing a large volume of materials in.

The day of the sale all books, DVD’s and CD’s will be .25 cents.  Magazines are 10 cents each or 12 for $1.

title: BUCHANAN SENTENCED
full_story:
Cody R. Buchanan, 35, of Geff was given a four-year sentence with the Illinois Department of Corrections (IDOC) Tuesday in Wayne County Court after he was found guilty of methamphetamine possession.

Associate Judge Denton Aud credited Buchanan with the 99 days he has served, and the judge imposed no new financial sentence.

At the beginning of June, Buchanan admitted to a violation of the two-year probation he was given in February 2025.  His case began in December 2025 when he was charged with meth possession and driving on a suspended license.

Two cases were dismissed for Buchanan on motions by the state Tuesday, including charges of meth and drug paraphernalia possession from July 2025 and a driving on a suspended license charge from March 2025.

title: GEFF FRONTIER DAYS
full_story:
Geff Frontier Days will be held next Saturday with more than 60 vendors expected to set up in the village park.  Organizer Julie Hall said there is an extraordinary vendor turnout offering crafts, food, antiques, farm products, homemade goods and other merchandise.

The Day begins with the Geff Ruritan breakfast at 7 am.  For children, Frog races begin at 9 am, followed by turtle races at 9:30 am.  A most-decorated baby contest and diaper derby will begin at 10 am, with a basketball shoot-out, sack and three-legged races, sawdust pile money hunt and pedal pull following throughout the day.

There will not be a Frontier Days parade this year, but the day’s schedule is packed with traditional events for children and adults to enjoy.  Frontier Days’ traditional ham and beans with cornbread will also be served beginning at 11:30 am in the Ruritan building, with the meal cooked over an open fire.  The quilt show will run from 8:30 am to 4 pm, with a quilting demonstration at the Town Hall at 10 am Car and tractor show registration begins at 9 am, and bingo starts at 2 pm.

Local entertainment is also planned throughout the day.  The Little Miss Geff Frontier Days Pageant for girls ages 6 to 9, will begin at 6 pm closing out the day.
